battle.name: 黃巢攻東都之戰
battle.brief: 廣明元年（880）十一月，黃巢自曹州西進，渡河後直趨洛陽——唐人稱洛陽為東都。外郭、皇城、紫微城三重城垣數日而陷，河南尹羅嗣英殉城，府庫軍器盡為亂軍所掠，叛軍遂以東都為西進關中的基地。卡面的羅馬弩砲並非唐代器械，它代表攻城投射火器的技術譜系：唐代攻城靠拋石、床弩、雲梯與撞木。

kit.name: 羅馬弩砲
kit.history: 扭力弩砲，一發一具箭。羅馬用它拆掉希臘的城牆，也拆掉了希臘的城邦體系。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰一方是唐僖宗的中和朝廷與河南府留守，另一方是黃巢率領的起義軍。中和朝廷一方守洛陽的，是河南尹羅嗣英所領的府兵與城內宿衛、監軍：洛陽自隋煬帝建東都以來即為陪都，外郭、皇城、紫微城三重城垣相套，城內有太廟、尚書省與府庫，儲著轉運天下粟帛的積儲與軍器。外圍援軍分佈在河中、昭義、忠武等道：河中節度使韓建、昭義節度使孟方立、忠武軍節度使張議郎各領本部兵馬奉詔赴援，或逗留觀望、或按兵自保，聯軍從無統一指揮，也沒有誰真的為保洛陽拼盡兵力。黃巢一方則是一支流動的起義軍：曹州起兵的鹽梟眾與王仙芝戰死後散入河南的餘眾合流，馬步輕捷而不耐攻城拔寨的消耗，攻洛陽時把沿途繳獲與裹挾的物資配成攻城器械隊，奪城之後就地補充糧秣與軍械。第三方是尚未入局的沙陀：此時李克用仍在北邊，朝廷屢下詔書請其出兵，而援軍未至，東都已先失。戰區的本質不是兩軍正面對撞，而是一場陪都與首都之間的信用競賽——東都握在誰手裡，關中的防線就往哪一邊傾斜，朝廷的每一次調兵都因此遲疑。東都的失守同時截斷一條漕運：江淮的粟帛自汴河、汴州轉入洛陽，再由洛陽西輸關中，陪都一陷，關中與江南之間的物資通道便成了一段斷口，朝廷連往後的補給都難以籌劃。
countriesEn: One side of this war was the Zhonghe court of Emperor Xianzong together with the Henan prefectural garrison, the other the rebel host led by Huang Chao. The court side that held Luoyang was the troops of Henan Yin Luo Siying together with the garrison within the walls and the imperial supervisors: since the Sui emperor Yang built the Eastern Capital, Luoyang had been the secondary capital of the empire, its outer city, imperial city and Palace City nested one within another, and inside it stood the imperial ancestral temple, the Department of State Affairs and the prefectural treasury, which held the grain and silk in transit from across the empire as well as the arms stores. The relief armies lay out along the circuits of Hezhong, Zhaoyi and Zhongwu: Hezhong's jiedushi Han Jian, Zhaoyi's Meng Fangli and Zhongwu's Zhang Yilang each led their own contingents by command of the court, but they hung back and watched, each preserving its own strength, and the coalition never had a unified command nor anyone prepared to spend his men in earnest to save Luoyang. Huang Chao's side was a fluid rebel host: the salt smugglers who rose at Caozhou merged with the remnants of Wang Xianzhi's army scattered across Henan after his death, light in horse and foot and impatient of the grinding work of reducing walled cities, and when they attacked Luoyang they organized what they had taken and carried on the march into a corps of siege equipment, replenishing grain and arms on the spot once the city fell. The third party was the Shatuo, still outside the game: Li Keyong was then in the north, the court issued summons after summons for him to bring troops, and the relief had not arrived when the Eastern Capital was already lost. The essence of this theatre was not a set-piece meeting of two armies but a contest of credibility between the secondary capital and the primary one: whichever side held the Eastern Capital tilted the defence of Guanzhong its way, and every dispatch of troops by the court was therefore delayed by doubt. The fall of the Eastern Capital also cut a canal route: the grain and silk of the Yangtze and Huai came up the Bian canal and through Bianzhou into Luoyang, and from Luoyang were carried west into Guanzhong; once the secondary capital fell, the line of supply between Jiangnan and the capital was broken in the middle, and the court could scarcely even plan its future resupply.
people: 兩端的關鍵人物都在關鍵位置上作過決定。黃巢字巨真，蒲州曹州冤句人，早年是往來各地販運私鹽的鹽梟；王仙芝於乾符二年在河南起事後，他聚眾響應，眾至數千，後與王仙芝合流，王仙芝其後戰死於河南，其部眾多歸黃巢，兵勢遂成。河南尹羅嗣英是洛陽城守的主持者，《資治通鑑》記其與城俱亡，是唐廷失守東都時唯一有姓名留存的守臣。僖宗李儇在亂軍西進時把軍國大政交給宦官田令孜，田令孜掌禁軍與神策，是唐廷手上最後一支能隨意調動的武力，也是僖宗西幸的直接推手；地方節度使韓建、孟方立、張議郎奉詔赴援而各懷算計，構成了唐廷救不出洛陽的真正原因。攻方陣中，黃巢之外有尚讓、葛從周等分將兵權，尚讓後來反噬舊主，葛從周則降唐，官軍得以收編其眾。真正改變整段戰局走向的是李克用，字鴉兒，出身河朔沙陀部；883 年初他率沙陀騎兵入關，於潼關大破巢軍，叛軍西走，884 年黃巢死於泰山狼虎谷。另一條線是朱溫與秦宗權：汴州猛將朱溫早年投入黃巢，歸唐後以收編降卒起家，秦宗權據蔡州而壯大，日後正是這一類人把唐朝推下懸崖。
peopleEn: The decisive men on both ends made their decisions where they stood. Huang Chao, courtesy name Juzhen, was a native of Yuanju in Caozhou in Puzhou who had made his living carrying illegal salt between regions; when Wang Xianzhi raised the standard in Henan in the second year of Qianfu, Huang Chao gathered men and answered the call, the multitude numbering several thousands, and later joined forces with Wang Xianzhi. when Wang Xianzhi died in Henan some time later, most of his followers went over to Huang Chao and the force took on its own momentum. Luo Siying, governor of Henan, directed the defence of Luoyang; the Zizhi Tongjian records that he died with the city, and he is the only defender of the Eastern Capital whose name survives. Emperor Xianzong handed the conduct of government to the eunuch Tian Lingzi as the rebel host advanced westward; Tian held the Imperial Guard and the Divine Might troops, the last body of troops the court could move at will, and he was the man who drove the emperor's flight west. The circuit governors Han Jian, Meng Fangli and Zhang Yilang came by command of the court yet each pursued his own interest, and together they are the real reason Luoyang could not be rescued. On the attacking side, apart from Huang Chao himself, Shang Rang and Ge Congzhou held separate commands; Shang Rang later turned on his old master, while Ge Congzhou surrendered to Tang, and the imperial troops were able to fold his men into their own ranks. The man who genuinely changed the course of the whole business was Li Keyong, courtesy name Ya'er, of the Shatuo of northern Hebei; in early 883 he brought the Shatuo cavalry into the pass and broke Huang Chao's army at Tongguan, the rebels were driven west, and in 884 Huang Chao was killed at Langhugu in Mount Tai. The other line is Zhu Wen and Qin Zongquan: Zhu Wen of Bianzhou, a fierce fighter, joined Huang Chao in his early years and built himself up after submitting to Tang by taking in surrendered men, while Qin Zongquan grew strong holding Caizhou; it was men of this kind who would push the Tang off the precipice.
kits: 卡面這具羅馬弩砲（Scorpio）是公元前五十年前後羅馬軍的制式火器：木製框架張以扭簧儲力，一發一矢，弩矢長度以公尺計、每具重可十餘公斤，機位由兩三人操作，可在一分鐘內連續發射數十發，有效射程在三百公尺上下。羅馬人把它用於野戰中壓制遠距目標，也用於攻城時封住城頭的射界；卡面所說「用它拆掉希臘的城牆」正是這層用法。放到八百八十年的洛陽，這具機器並不在場。唐代東都的攻城，實際動用的是三類器材：一是拋石，唐人稱「砲」，以木臂或配重把石彈拋向城頭、砸向城牆，這是攻破城防的主力；二是弩機，安在床架上的大型弩車與小床弩，以絞盤張弦，射程遠而射速慢；三是雲梯、巢車與撞木這類近身器材，供步兵攀城與破門。守方則以弓弩、礪石、檑木與飛火應對，並靠三重城垣的縱深換取時間。相比之下，羅馬弩砲那種以扭簧儲能、單發重箭、可高速連發的機械弩，在中國並沒有相應的實物技術路徑——唐弩以絞盤與人力蓄力，無扭簧；兩者只是同屬「機械弩」這一門類。卡面用羅馬弩砲代表這門類在羅馬體系裡最成熟的形態，用以標明本役攻防雙方的火力配置：一方靠拋石砸、一方靠弩射，羅馬式的單發扭力火器留在技術譜系的位置上。運輸與畜力方面，府庫的軍器與糧秣靠漕船自江淮轉運入洛，牛車與騾隊負責城內外的短途搬運；起義軍以馬匹為主，攻城器械多靠沿途繳獲與徵用，奪城之後就地取用被守軍遺棄的器械與糧食。洛陽三重城垣之間有洛水貫城，浮橋與水門本身就是城防的一部分：攻城者要跨水而入，器械便難以一次鋪開；守方則可藉水門與橋梁反覆出人。這種以水道分割的城防，是羅馬軍攻城時同樣面對過的難題——但羅馬人手中有一具可以架在城下的單發扭力火器，唐軍這裡只有靠人力絞盤張弦的弩機與配重拋石。
kitsEn: The Roman bolt-thrower on the card (Scorpio) was standard artillery in the Roman army around 50 BC: a wooden frame wound with torsion springs that stored the energy, one heavy bolt to a shot, the bolts measured in metres and weighing some ten-odd kilograms each, the piece served by two or three men and able to fire dozens of shots a minute with an effective range of around three hundred metres. The Romans used it both to bear down on distant targets in the field and to seal the firing positions on a wall during a siege, and the card's remark that it was used to break down the walls of Greek cities points exactly at that use. Set at Luoyang in the year 880, this machine was not present. Tang siegecraft at the Eastern Capital actually worked with three kinds of equipment. First, thrown stone: the Tang called it the po, a stone-thrower using a timber arm or a counterweight to lob a stone ball at the wall-head or against the wall, and this was the main means of breaking defences. Second, bolt-throwers: large crossbow engines mounted on bed frames and smaller bed crossbows, drawn by windlass, long-ranged but slow in rate of fire. Third, the close-range gear of scaling ladders, siege towers and battering rams, for infantry to climb and for gates to be broken. The defenders answered with bows and crossbows, stone missiles, dropped logs and fire-pots, and bought time from the depth of their threefold walls. The Roman engine's way of storing power in torsion springs, firing a single heavy bolt and repeating quickly, had no corresponding physical technological line in China: Tang crossbows were wound by windlass and muscle, with no torsion springs; the two belong to the same category of mechanical crossbow and no more. The card uses the Roman ballista to represent the most developed form of that category in the Roman system, and thereby to mark the configuration of firepower on both sides in this campaign: one side smashed with thrown stone, the other shot with crossbows, while the Roman single-shot torsion piece stayed at the level of technological pedigree. For transport and motive power, the arms and grain in the treasury came up to Luoyang by canal barge from the Yangtze and Huai, with ox carts and mule teams handling the short hauls inside and outside the walls; the rebel host travelled on horseback, its siege gear mostly taken by capture and requisition on the march, and after the city fell it simply used the equipment and food the defenders abandoned. Between the threefold walls of Luoyang the Luo river ran through the city, and its floating bridges and water gates were themselves part of the defences: an attacker had to cross the water, so his equipment could not be brought up all at once, while the defenders could move men back and forth by the water gates and the bridges. A defence cut into pieces by waterways was a difficulty Roman armies met as well, but the Romans had a single-shot torsion piece they could set up below the wall, whereas the Tang here had only windlass-drawn crossbow engines and counterweight stone-throwers.
tactics: 本役的戰法分為進逼、攻城與斷援三段。進逼一段，黃巢不與唐軍主力正面合戰，而是以輕騎縱掠河南平原，掃掉沿途城縣的守兵，切斷自江淮入洛的漕運與糧道，把洛陽變成一座糧援不繼的孤城；沿途繳獲的牛羊、糧食與器械就地編入攻城隊伍，這是流動軍隊能夠打陪都的唯一辦法。攻城一段，兵力集中於外郭城一面：拋石反覆投向城牆與城頭，雲梯與巢車靠上去時以弓弩掩護，撞木對準城門，最終由內應與衝擊配合破門而入；守方以三重城垣逐層抵抗，外郭既陷，退守皇城，再退入紫微城，但每一層抵抗都在消耗糧秣與器械，最終難免陷落。斷援一段，黃巢的騎兵在洛陽周邊與官道一線游走，使各道援軍不敢合兵；唐廷雖連下詔書，河中、昭義、忠武的兵馬各守本位、彼此牽制，聯軍始終無法形成攻勢，救援從一開始就是各自算計的一盤散沙。全役的成敗因此不取決於某一場會戰，而取決於三件事的先後：叛軍的攻城器械何時湊齊、漕運的糧道何時被切斷、各道援軍何時願意拿出真本錢。洛陽城南一帶地勢平曠，極利於騎兵展開與拋石布陣，這是叛軍把攻城與野戰合為一體的地理基礎；反過來，城內外河道交錯、橋梁可拆，攻城器械一旦被守軍以舟船封住水路，便只能逐段使用，戰力難以一次壓上。
tacticsEn: The method of this campaign had three movements: the advance, the assault on the walls, and the cutting of relief. In the advance, Huang Chao declined to meet the Tang field army head-on, sweeping the Henan plain with light cavalry, clearing the garrisons of the towns and counties on the way, cutting the canal traffic and grain route that fed Luoyang from the Yangtze and Huai, and turning the Eastern Capital into a city cut off from its supplies; the cattle, food and equipment taken along the march were folded on the spot into the assault corps, which was the only way a mobile host could take a secondary capital. In the assault, the strength was concentrated on one face of the outer city: thrown stones were directed again and again at the wall and the wall-head, scaling ladders and siege towers went up under cover of bows and crossbows, rams were set against the gates, and the wall was finally carried by a combination of work from within and a rush from without. The defenders resisted tier by tier through the threefold walls, falling back from the outer city to the imperial city and then into the Palace City, but each tier of resistance consumed grain and equipment, and the end was inevitable. In the third movement, the rebel horsemen patrolled the country around Luoyang and along the official roads so that the relief armies of the various circuits would dare not concentrate; the court issued summons after summons, but the troops of Hezhong, Zhaoyi and Zhongwu each stayed on their own ground and checked one another, the coalition never formed an offensive, and the relief was from the outset a handful of separate calculations. The outcome of the whole campaign therefore turned not on any single battle but on the order of three things: when the rebel siege equipment could be assembled, when the grain route by canal would be cut, and when the armies of the circuits would finally put real men on the table. The ground south of Luoyang was flat and open, extremely favourable to deploying cavalry and emplacing the stone-throwers, and this was the geographical basis on which the rebels fused the siege and the field battle into one operation; conversely, with waterways crossing in and out of the city and bridges that could be cut, the attacker's siege equipment, once the defenders sealed the water with boats, could only be brought up section by section and its strength could not be applied all at once.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。時序上，乾符二年（875）王仙芝在河南起事，其後兩年黃巢合流；廣明元年（880）十月起義軍西進，十一月抵洛陽城下，數日之間城破；其後潼關、華州相繼失守，華州刺史畢師安以城降；十二月叛軍入長安，僖宗出奔鳳翔，其後西幸成都；黃巢入京師後建國號大齊、改元金統（年號所繫年份，各家記載略有出入）；八百八十三年正月李克用率沙陀騎兵破巢軍於潼關，巢焚長安宮室而走，保據蔡州；八百八十四年六月至七月，黃巢敗走泰山狼虎谷，為部下所殺，諸子亦死。地理量度上，曹州至洛陽約八百里，洛陽至潼關沿官道約六百餘里，潼關至長安約二百餘里；自洛陽經潼關至長安合計約八九百里，騎兵疾行亦需十餘日，這是叛軍自東都直逼關中所需時間的下限。洛陽城舊志約記周長十八里有奇，外郭、皇城、紫微城三重相套。兵力方面，黃巢軍在鼎盛時諸史所記從數萬到數十萬不等，甚至有「百萬」之辭，歷代史家多以為號稱之數有誇，實際投入攻城與野戰者或在數萬至十餘萬之間，各家記載互異；沙陀騎兵通稱數千，具體人數諸說紛紜；勤王聯軍來自十數道，總數無可考的實數。攻城器械的數目、雙方陣亡與俘虜的總數，兩《唐書》與《資治通鑑》都沒有留下可核的數字，不宜當作數據使用；此役的記載本來就以行軍方向、援兵態度和城破先後為主，數字多從缺。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are roughly these. In chronology: Wang Xianzhi rose in Henan in the second year of Qianfu, 875, and Huang Chao merged with him two years later; the rebel host moved west in the tenth month of 880 and stood beneath the walls of Luoyang in the eleventh, the city falling within days; in the months that followed Tongguan and Huazhou were lost one after another, the prefect of Huazhou Bi Shi'an surrendering the city; in the twelfth month the rebels entered Chang'an and the emperor fled to Fengxiang and later to Chengdu, and Huang Chao, now in the imperial city, proclaimed the Great Qi and changed the era to Jintong (the year to which the era is tied differs slightly between the accounts); in the first month of 883 Li Keyong broke the rebel army at Tongguan with the Shatuo cavalry, and Huang Chao burned the palace of Chang'an and withdrew to hold at Caizhou; between the sixth and seventh months of 884 he was driven to Langhugu in Mount Tai and killed by his own men, and his sons died with the cause. In geography: Caozhou to Luoyang is about eight hundred li, and along the official road Luoyang to Tongguan is about six hundred and more li, with Tongguan to Chang'an a little over two hundred li; from Luoyang through Tongguan to Chang'an comes to some eight or nine hundred li in all, a horse at a gallop taking a dozen days or more, and that is the lower limit of the time the rebels needed to drive from the Eastern Capital at the heart of Guanzhong. The old gazetteer gives the circuit of Luoyang as about eighteen li and more, its outer city, imperial city and Palace City nested one within another. In strength: at its height the rebel host is given in the histories as running from tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands, with even a claim of a million, and successive historians have held that the self-reported figures are inflated, the men actually committed to the assault and to field fighting lying somewhere between several tens of thousands and a hundred-odd thousand, with the accounts differing; the Shatuo cavalry are commonly given as several thousand, the exact number given variously; the relief coalition drew from a dozen circuits and no checkable total exists. The number of siege engines and the totals of dead and prisoners on both sides leave no checkable figure in the two Tang histories or the Zizhi Tongjian and should not be used as data; the record of this campaign simply runs on lines of march, the bearing of the relief armies and the order in which the city fell, and numbers are largely absent.
cause: 開戰的動因，是鹽法與饑荒釀成的流民洪流，遇上削藩逼出的藩鎮反亂。乾符以來兩池鹽法嚴苛，私鹽販運的隊伍越聚越大，這些人半是走私者、半是亡命之徒；王仙芝、尚讓、黃巢相繼起事，攻城掠地而不圖久守，河北、河南一帶連歲不登，州縣倉儲空虛，朝廷的賑濟與賑兵卻杯水車薪，大量無業流民湧入起義軍隊伍，使軍數在兩三年之間膨脹到數十萬。朝廷自身的處置則把局勢推向失控：僖宗即位後一心削藩，屢罷方鎮、換將吏，逼得擁兵自重者反亂；各道節度使奉詔出兵卻各保實力，遇敗則互相推諿，遇勝則各分其功，勤王之師人數再多也打不成一仗。洛陽正是這盤散沙最要命的位置：它是漕運入關的終點與陪都所在，東都一失，關中與江南之間的糧線與政令中樞同時斷裂，朝廷連一個能統一指揮的側面都組織不起來。朝臣與宦官互疑、軍令出而節度使不行，亦是勤王之師貌合神離的一層原因：詔書到了各道，如何調度、幾時出兵的解釋權，實際落在受命者手裡。
causeEn: What set this war going was a flood of displaced people bred by the salt laws and by famine, meeting the separatist risings that the court's own reduction policy had provoked. The salt monopoly of the two northern depots had grown harsh since Qianfu, and the gangs carrying illegal salt grew larger all the while, half smugglers and half men with nothing to lose. Wang Xianzhi, Shang Rang and Huang Chao rose in turn, taking cities and country without any thought of holding what they took, and in the Hebei and Henan regions harvests failed year after year, the granaries of the prefectures stood empty, and the court's relief money and relief troops were a drop in the ocean; a great many people with no livelihood poured into the rebel ranks, and the host swelled to tens of thousands within two or three years. The court's own handling of the situation then drove things out of control. After his accession Xianzong made the reduction of the circuits his single policy, dismissing governors and changing officers again and again, and those who held troops for themselves rose in revolt; the circuit governors came by command of the court yet each preserved his own strength, deflecting blame after defeat and dividing the credit after success, so that however many troops the relief mustered they never fought as one. Luoyang was precisely the fatal point in that scatter: it was the terminus of the canal traffic into Guanzhong and the seat of the secondary capital, and once the Eastern Capital fell the grain line and the administrative heart between Jiangnan and the capital were cut at the same moment, leaving the court unable even to organise one flank under a single command. The mutual suspicion of ministers and eunuchs, and orders issued that the circuit governors simply did not obey, formed a further layer in the relief army's outward unity and inward division: once a rescript reached a circuit, the power to decide how to move and when to march lay in the hands of the man who had received it.
impact: 東都陷落的影響，遠大於一場攻城戰本身。第一是秩序層面的：洛陽的宮室、府庫、太廟與漕運積儲在數日之內易手，朝廷在關中的補給線自此要繞道，僖宗被迫西幸鳳翔、成都，帝王的車駕第一次長久地離開京師，天下的觀感由此轉向。第二是軍制層面的：平亂倚賴沙陀騎兵，李克用因此得以坐大河東，率軍鎮之力問鼎中央；朝廷為制衡藩鎮，反而不斷倚重這支客軍，救命的倚賴再一次落在另一個方鎮手裡。第三是權力版圖層面的：巢軍失敗之後，朱溫、秦宗權等人以討巢為名各據一方，把原本的亂軍收編為私兵，朝廷平了叛亂，卻替藩鎮清除了障礙。908 年朱溫代唐，二百八十九年的唐朝告終，五代十國的分裂開局由此奠定。東都本身則淪為廢墟，直到中唐以後才漸次恢復舊觀；一座陪都的存亡，最後成了唐廷中央權威的量度。洛陽城破之後，官署、寺觀與倉儲多被亂軍所毀，東都的市面與元氣一時難以恢復，其後數十年竟不如開元、天寶之盛，直到唐末仍未能完全復舊。
impactEn: The fall of the Eastern Capital mattered far more than the storming of a city. First in the sphere of order: the palace halls, the treasury, the imperial ancestral temple and the grain in transit at Luoyang changed hands within a few days, the court's supply line into Guanzhong had to be bent from that moment on, and the emperor was driven west to Fengxiang and Chengdu; the imperial carriage was long absent from the capital for the first time, and the mood of the realm turned accordingly. Second in the sphere of the military system: the suppression of the rebellion rested on the Shatuo cavalry, so Li Keyong was able to grow strong in Hedong and bring the weight of a circuit army to bear on the centre; and because the court needed a counterweight to the separatist governors, it went on leaning on that foreign army, so that the dependence on which its survival rested passed once again into the hands of another circuit. Third in the sphere of the map of power: after the rebel host was beaten, men such as Zhu Wen and Qin Zongquan took up the cause of fighting Huang Chao as a pretext and each held a region of their own, folding the disorderly troops of the rebellion into their private forces; in defeating the rising the court cleared the ground for the circuits instead. In 908 Zhu Wen took the throne from the Tang, the dynasty of two hundred and eighty-nine years ended, and the divided age of the Five Dynasties and the Ten Kingdoms was thereby set in motion. Luoyang itself was reduced to ruins and recovered something of its old appearance only gradually in the later middle Tang; the survival of a secondary capital became, in the end, a measure of the court's central authority. After the city fell the offices, temples and granaries of Luoyang were largely wrecked by the rebels, and the life of the Eastern Capital could not be restored at once; for several decades afterwards it did not equal the height of the Kaiyuan and Tianbao years, and it was never fully made good before the Tang's end.
result: 結果是東都攻陷與起義的最終覆亡。廣明元年十一月，黃巢大軍破洛陽外郭，河南尹羅嗣英與城俱亡，守軍潰散，府庫的軍器、糧秣與財貨盡為亂軍所取，叛軍以東都為基地西進；同月潼關、華州相繼失守，十二月入長安，僖宗出奔，黃巢建大齊、改元金統。然而攻陷東都並不等於得天下：關中無糧可支，各道援兵不為所用，叛軍的攻城器械雖盛，騎兵雖銳，卻守不住關中的關隘與城防。八百八十三年正月，李克用率沙陀騎兵入關，潼關一戰巢軍大敗，黃巢焚長安宮室而走，保據蔡州；八百八十四年，黃巢敗走泰山狼虎谷，為自己部將所殺，大齊的號令自此終結，餘眾或降或散。八百八十三年末，僖宗自成都還都長安，重建朝廷典禮。東都則回到唐廷手中，卻已是一座空城：宮室焚毀、倉廩空虛，漕運未復而藩鎮尾大不掉，收拾這副殘局用去朝廷剩餘的全部元氣。
resultEn: The result was the fall of the Eastern Capital and, in the end, the destruction of the rebellion. In the eleventh month of 880 Huang Chao's host broke the outer city of Luoyang; Luo Siying, governor of Henan, died with the city, the garrison broke up, and the arms, grain and money in the treasury were taken by the rebels, who used the Eastern Capital as a base for their drive west. In the same month Tongguan and Huazhou were lost, and in the twelfth month the rebels entered Chang'an, the emperor fled, and Huang Chao proclaimed the Great Qi and changed the era to Jintong. Taking the Eastern Capital, however, was not the same as taking the empire: Guanzhong had no grain to support an army, the troops of the circuits would not combine, and though the rebel siege equipment was plentiful and their cavalry sharp, they could not hold the passes and the walled cities of Guanzhong. In the first month of 883 Li Keyong brought the Shatuo cavalry into the pass and the rebel army was broken at Tongguan; Huang Chao burned the palace of Chang'an and withdrew to hold at Caizhou, and in 884 he was driven to Langhugu in Mount Tai and killed by his own commander, so that the Great Qi proclaimed at Chaozhou came to an end, its remnant men surrendering or scattering. At the end of 883 the emperor returned from Chengdu to the capital and the ceremonies of the court were restored. The Eastern Capital returned to the Tang, but it was an empty city: the palace halls burned, the granaries bare, the canal traffic unrepaired while the circuits grew ever more overbearing, and the court spent all the strength it had left in picking up the pieces.
